_about: Wire contract consumed by Milo-iOS (github.com/leodurandfr/Milo-iOS), a THIRD API client beyond frontend/ and Milo-Mac. Its consumers are short-lived processes — a WidgetKit timeline entry, App Intents — so there is NO WebSocket surface at all: everything is REST, and the app can never be told about a change, only ask. If a route listed here is dropped, Milo-iOS breaks silently at runtime. THIS FILE IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH for that contract. test_milo_ios_contract.py enforces it offline on every pytest run: the backend still serves every route in `rest`, the manifest matches the VENDORED snapshot's surface exactly, and every payload_invariant holds against the typed response models. check_milo_ios_freshness.py is run BY HAND against a checkout (there is no CI job; 56a3263f dropped it) and refuses to compare at all when a route literal lives outside the vendored file patterns. Refresh the snapshot and this file TOGETHER, consciously, in one commit.
_surface_is_declared_not_reached: The extractor reads the routes MiloAPIClient DECLARES, which is the right granularity for a contract — the app ships that code, and a backend free to delete a route it targets is the hazard. Both ends of that policy have now been measured. `getAudioState` was declared and called by nothing, was pinned anyway, and a84400a9 gave it a caller when the Now Playing extension began reading the active source before every transport command: pinning it while nothing called it is what kept the route alive until something did. `getDockApps` was the other standing example and went the other way — the app DELETED the declaration at 741f8dc1, so the pin left with it. That is the policy working, not an exception to it: the contract follows what the client declares, in both directions, and neither side ever had to guess what the other intended.
_why_this_exists: cf430ae6 deleted GET /api/settings/dock-apps as 'Milo-Mac-only' once the Mac had converged on /bulk. Milo-iOS' client layer targeted it too, and nothing in this checkout recorded that. The break was latent rather than live — no caller reached getDockApps in the published build — so nobody was broken; the point is that nobody could have known either way. A route with no caller in frontend/src/ is not dead, it is unwitnessed. RESOLVED at Milo-iOS 741f8dc1, which deleted getDockApps and DockAppsResponse: the dependency is gone rather than papered over, and this file is what made it visible enough to delete deliberately. The reasoning survives the entry — it is why a THIRD client earns a manifest at all.
_no_tolerance_sections: `_broken_calls` lived here until 741f8dc1 and held exactly one route — GET /api/settings/dock-apps, which the app targeted and the backend answered 405. It was never a weakened assertion: it was data whose own test failed the moment either side moved, so it could not become a permanent exemption, and it self-deleted the moment Milo-iOS dropped the call. The doctrine outlives the section and is the reason it is recorded here rather than removed with it: NEVER ADD A SECTION OF THIS KIND TO PAPER OVER A MISMATCH. Two have existed and both are gone. `_pending_push` let the manifest lead the published app while a batch of routes was in flight; the batch was cancelled and the tolerance would have outlived its reason. `_broken_calls` was legitimate because it described a defect that already existed and could not be silent — and because its test would fail if the defect were ever fixed, which is what happened. A tolerance that cannot fail on its own is not a contract, it is a comment. The contract is a plain equality: manifest == snapshot, in both directions. If a genuine broken call reappears, restore the section AND the test that proves it is still broken — test_a_tolerance_section_brings_its_test_back fails until you do.

_snapshot.eighteen_commits_of_drift: This refresh crossed a84400a9 -> be15c1f, and the manifest was wrong the whole way: FOUR routes the app declared were in no section of it (PATCH /api/volume/global, GET /api/multiroom/state, POST /api/push/sessions, GET /api/radio/stations). Every call still goes through MiloAPIClient — the Intents and the widget's timeline provider build no URL of their own — but it is no longer ONE file: 09b9789b put the push routes in MiloAPIClient+Push.swift, and Now Playing will add more extensions.
_snapshot.content_stale_while_the_surface_matched: 741f8dc1 -> 0edead3, refreshed with NO surface change and for the reason `refreshed_without_a_surface_change` already names: the vendored copy would have misled a reader. 0b69b6a fixed five defects in the app's Now Playing volume path, including an absorbing zero, adding 146 lines to MiloAPIClient+Media.swift and 6 to MiloNowPlayingBridge.swift — but no route and no decoded field moved, so check_milo_ios_freshness.py answered 'matches upstream, 5 files, 12 routes' and was right to. Nothing can see this automatically: the script compares extracted SURFACES and never contents, and `manifest == snapshot` compares the manifest to the stale copy. It was found by diffing the two vendored files against a fresh clone by hand, while deciding what PushService._signature should carry — the same volume path, read from the other side. When you clone to run the script, diff the files too.
_snapshot.three_refreshes_in_two_days_is_not_a_sch: 4b9e73f -> 3018b8f, and the frequency is the thing worth answering: 741f8dc1 -> 0edead3 -> 4b9e73f -> 3018b8f is three refreshes inside two days, which looks exactly like the per-commit habit the test below refuses. It is not one, and the difference is that each was taken for a reader who would have been told something false. This one: the vendored bridge held a guard whose comment promised that a metadata hole under a playing source would not close the session, while the expression read `is_playing` out of the very dictionary its own first half requires to be empty — always true when evaluated, so the promise was never kept. Written that way since 8c8feef, moved and re-documented by 4b9e73f without anyone seeing it, removed at 6b252b0 because there was nothing to repair: an empty metadata cannot say whether anything plays, and `source_state` is the only witness left. A backend reader opening this file to learn when the app drops the card would have read that an ACTIVE source with empty metadata closes it — false, and false for a real state, since a source can go ACTIVE before its first metadata. Same shape as the `development` entitlement precedent below: wrong code, on the one file consulted for that very question. 3018b8f rides along and moves no surface either — `buildState` became `buildAttributes(from:)` and `refresh()` now reads /api/audio/state itself, same route, same file, same call shape. check_milo_ios_freshness.py answered `matches upstream, 5 files, 12 routes` before and after, and four of the five files came back byte-identical. The rule stays what it says: refresh when the content would mislead, or when the surface moved — never because time passed, and never because a commit happened.
_snapshot.the_rule_the_backend_had_just_invalidate: 0edead3 -> 4b9e73f, the second content-only refresh in two days and the first where the BACKEND is what moved. 95293764 made a stopped mpv source publish what a play press would resume — the station resume_playback re-tunes, the episode an auto-stop left — so `source_state: ready` stopped meaning `nothing to show`. MiloNowPlayingBridge still ended the Lock Screen session on `sourceState != "active"`, which closed the card on exactly those resumable stops; 4b9e73f replaced that with a conjunction whose second half is _displays_something's own predicate, read off the same `metadata.title` and nothing else. The vendored copy therefore stated, on the one file a backend reader would open to check what the app does with source_state, the rule this repo had just invalidated — the `would mislead a reader` half of the test below, arrived from the far side. No route and no decoded field moved: check_milo_ios_freshness.py answered `matches upstream, 5 files, 12 routes` before and after, and four of the five vendored files came back byte-identical. Measured on the device 2026-09-22: station stopped, backend published ready + title, the app held session e25574e6 across the stop instead of closing it, Milō ended that session 300s later on its own schedule, and the app declined to reopen one (`aucune session, et rien à ouvrir`) because openSession still guards on isPlaying — Milō owns the lifecycle, the app only declines to end it early.
_snapshot.refreshed_without_a_surface_change: Was true three times, 09b9789b -> 5e70b79 -> c4cea32b -> efef56dc, when no route moved: MiloAPIClient.swift and Models.swift are byte-identical and only MiloAPIClient+Push.swift changed. Refreshed anyway because the vendored copy still held the version that sent the raw `development` entitlement value and took a 422 — a reader consulting it to learn what the app sends would have read code that was wrong, on the very file where that trap occurred. This is NOT a rule to refresh per commit: the test is whether the vendored content would mislead a reader, or whether the surface moved. `check_milo_ios_freshness.py` cannot decide it either way — it compares extracted surfaces, never contents.
_snapshot.why_patterns_not_a_list: The previous snapshot listed exactly two filenames. When the app gained POST /api/push/tokens and DELETE /api/push/tokens/{} in a third file, the extractor read an unchanged surface and the freshness script printed 'vendored snapshot matches upstream' — the contract passing by describing an app that no longer existed, which is the one rot mode _broken_calls.why names. rest.note: Body {delta_db, show_bar}. Built by hand with URLRequest rather than the get/post helper — the extractor reads both shapes on purpose.

Milo-iOS reads THREE fields here and no others — volume_limits.min_db, volume_limits.max_db, volume_steps.step_mobile_db — all of them in syncVolumeSettings, by hand off a JSONSerialization dict rather than through a Codable. The response ALSO carries dock_apps.enabled_apps, and this app does not read it: `enabled_apps` occurs in Milo-iOS only inside Models.swift::DockAppsResponse, which is decoded from GET /api/settings/dock-apps in `_broken_calls`, and `dock_apps` occurs in the app nowhere at all. It was nevertheless listed as a payload_invariant on THIS route until 2026-09-20 — the attribution mistake payload_invariants._about now describes. The field is real and load-bearing, just for other clients: frontend/src/stores/settingsStore.js and Milo-Mac's fetchBulkSettings both read it.

TWO consumers, both through Shared/MiloAudioState.swift since 39b0de28: MiloAPIClient+Media.activeSource() reads the state before every transport command, because /api/audio/control addresses a NAMED source and there is no command to the system; MiloNowPlayingBridge.refresh() polls the SAME route every two seconds while the app is foreground and builds the Lock Screen card from it — the card exists while `session` or `resume` carries a `title` (MiloAudioState.shown, the same rule as PushService._displays_something), `isPlaying` is `session.phase == playing`, elapsed time and timestamp come from `session.position` (the anchor), and `phase == connected` draws « Connecté à X » from `session.senders`. The decoder requires `source`, `switching`, `service`, `controls` and the two flags, and inside a session `id`, `phase` and `senders`: a missing one fails the whole decode, which the app treats as an unreadable state (traced apart from an unreachable Milō) and leaves the card as it was. `service` and `session.phase` are frozen enums. The keys are pinned by the schema invariant below, resolved against the typed AudioStateResponse (= core/models/audio_wire.py::AudioState). `details` is decoded leniently and is not pinned: it is a union the schema walker cannot resolve, and nothing in this app reads it beyond the decoder's own switch. Models.swift::AudioStateResponse still exists and is still used by nothing.

Registers one APNs token (widget / push_to_start / session). Called on every launch; idempotent, so a repeat is free. The app decodes ONE BODY FIELD, `status`, against 'success' — hence the single payload_invariant. Since c4cea32b it ALSO reads the HTTP status and answers registered / refused(detail) / unavailable, keeping a 4xx body verbatim: a 4xx is a verdict on the request, not a transient failure, so it is recorded and never replayed, while a network failure is retried. A refusal is remembered against the token it was about, so a fresh token lifts it. Two call sites reach that retry (didFinishLaunching and didRegisterForRemoteNotifications) and the guard around it is in-flight-aware since efef56dc — read-then-network-then-write left a window where both passed, and an actor did not close it because `await` in an actor method releases isolation. Measured against a stub that refuses: two POSTs became one. Milō could not see it over HTTP — both registrations are idempotent and both answer 200 — but the registry logs every register at INFO, so the duplicate WAS in the journal. The status code is deliberately NOT a payload_invariant: those are resolved by walking this route's OpenAPI RESPONSE SCHEMA, where a status code has no node at all. NOTE on `environment`: this API names the APNs HOSTS (sandbox | production), while Apple's aps-environment entitlement spells the same two values development | production. Milo-iOS forwarded the entitlement verbatim and took a 422 (fixed client-side in 5e70b79, which is where that translation belongs). At the time this client decoded only `status`, so the 422 was indistinguishable from a network failure and the registration silently never happened — that second half is what c4cea32b fixed, and it is why this note now describes a client that can see a refusal. The backend does not accept both spellings: one concept, one key.

Now Playing transport (play/pause/next/prev/seek) from the lock screen. Addressed to the source named by a fresh GET /api/audio/state, since this route takes a source and there is no command to the system. Decodes NOTHING — not the body, not the status code: it is fire-and-forget, and the authoritative state comes back in the next Now Playing push rather than in this reply, so a lost command corrects itself on the following update. No payload_invariants for that reason.

One Control Center slider per room. Each entry of the push payload's `devices` maps here; a burst touching two or more sliders at once is the MASTER handle and goes to PATCH /api/volume/global instead, which is a route this manifest missed for eighteen commits. Body {volume}, 0..1 over the operator's limits — the app no longer converts anything. That is the fix, and the paragraph this note used to carry is the bug it fixes: 'the app denormalizes the 0..1 it was sent back to dB using volume_limits from /api/settings/bulk … a write made against stale limits is rejected, the slider springs back on the next push, and nothing says why'. The danger was written down here before it happened, and then it happened on the GLOBAL slider, where nothing rejects: the unit clamps, so a level computed on a cached -80..-21 against a live -78..-8 simply landed somewhere else. `volume_db` is still accepted on this route for the web UI and Milo-Mac, and the two are mutually exclusive. Reads `volume` back — the applied level, which is what the slider shows for three seconds while the next push is in flight.

The master Control Center slider, in ONE request. Body {volume, show_bar}, 0..1, reads `volume` back. Three concurrent per-client writes also reach the right average — measured — but each posts a level it computed on its own side and the balance between rooms drifts with every gesture; `set_volume_db` shifts every client by one delta under `_volume_lock`, which is the only place that can be atomic. Declared by the app since b09ce77 and pinned only now. THE ROUTE TAKES NO DECIBELS: it has no dB caller anywhere (frontend/ moves the volume with /api/volume/adjust deltas, and the rotary, the IR remote and the Pi screen reach VolumeService without HTTP), so keeping a second scale on it would have kept alive exactly the divergence this commit removes.

Reads `clients[mac].name` and NOTHING else — the lock screen needs a per-room label and /api/volume/state names only zones, so two speakers in one zone both drew 'Salon'. No payload_invariant, and that is a limit of the walker rather than an omission: MultiroomStateResponse.clients is Dict[str, Any] (the client dataclass carries computed and conditional keys), so `clients[mac].name` has no node in the OpenAPI schema to resolve against. Typing the whole client model to pin one field would be a larger promise than the app makes. Declared in MiloNowPlayingBridge.swift, which is why that file is vendored: it is not named like a client file and its two route literals were invisible to the patterns until unvendored_surface reported them.

What the phone still holds. A session token outlives its session and only the device can tell the two apart, so this is the report that retires a ghost; an empty session_ids list is the most useful case, not a degenerate one. Decodes nothing. Prior drift — declared by the app well before this refresh, pinned only now.

Called with ?favorites_only=true; `_shape` strips the query, which is not part of the path contract. Warms the artwork cache for the widget. Prior drift — pinned only now. Milo-Mac pins the same route for its own favourites menu.

Decodes NOTHING from the body — it reads the HTTP status alone and treats 200 AND 404 alike, since a token the backend does not hold is already in the wanted state. No payload_invariants on purpose: asserting a field the app never reads would invent a contract instead of recording one. Hand-built URL with httpMethod = DELETE, the second call shape.

payload_invariants._about: The response fields Milo-iOS decodes by name. The three `data.clients[mac].*` entries are what MiloNowPlayingBridge.buildDevices reads to draw one slider per room: the level on the same scale Milō pushes, and the two flags it filters on — so the list the app builds while it is awake is the same list the APNs push carries while it sleeps, which is also the set Milō averages into its global level. A route can survive while the field the app reads is renamed, and a Codable struct missing a non-optional key throws rather than degrading — the whole call fails, it does not lose one value. Resolved through the live OpenAPI schema, never a hand-written copy: `a.b` is a property, `a[k]` a dict value (additionalProperties). ONE DIRECTION IS MACHINE-CHECKED AND ONE IS NOT, and the difference is the whole hazard here. test_schema_payload_invariant resolves each field against the BACKEND, so an invariant naming a field the backend does not serve fails. Nothing resolved it against the CLIENT, so an invariant naming a field the backend serves and the app never decodes passed forever — which is what `dock_apps.enabled_apps` did on /api/settings/bulk from the day it was written until 2026-09-20. It was invented from the backend side: bulk carries the field, so it looked true, and the only reader who could have refuted it is the Swift. test_an_invariant_names_a_key_the_app_mentions closes the cheap half: every wire key named here must occur as a token in the vendored snapshot. It catches a key the app never mentions AT ALL (`dock_apps` occurs zero times), which is how this one entered. It does NOT check ATTRIBUTION — that a key the app does mention is decoded from THIS route. `enabled_apps` occurs once, in DockAppsResponse, off a different route, and the guard cannot tell. Attribution lives in Swift's type graph, not in any literal, and the corpus decodes three ways (hand-read JSON keys in syncVolumeSettings, Codable structs in Models.swift, cross-file readers like MiloNowPlayingBridge reading clients[mac].* off a route declared on getVolume); a Python resolver for that would be the kind of extractor that degrades in silence, which is the failure this whole directory exists to prevent. So: presence is enforced, attribution is a HAND check, and it is owed once per refresh — read the consumer named on the route and confirm it decodes each field listed here.
